# V14 selected Amin: correct ledger, failed preservation

All18 preregistered family games completed before interpretation (Amin11453 exit0; external2293 exit0 reported by root). This report covers six Amin games on **one consumed placement with both seat/spawn-label mirrors**, not a fresh independent strength sample.

| Policy | Mirrored outcomes | Terminal turn |
|---|---|---:|
| V10 | 2 wins | 1033 |
| V10-v6 | 2 losses | 370 |
| V14 | 2 losses | 524 |

V10-v6 is weaker on this Amin placement despite advantages elsewhere. V14 fails to retain the best control's win. There is no promotion or dominance claim.

## Original execution and service allocation

All3,854 candidate frames retain original wires, raw/applied actions, keys, scalar telemetry and sequential19/7/20-field memory. Both controls exactly reproduce archived full raw histories; V10 also matches its prior original memory record. V10-v6 memory is newly recorded. Every V14 ledger transition and parent/reference attribution passes the independent arithmetic check. Per mirror:86 collection charges,86 debt units repaid, maximum debt6, final debt0, no resets. The264 eligible service moves include178 at zero debt. Balanced debt is bookkeeping, not tactical success.

The53 actual deferrals produce25 enemy attacks,1 neutral attack and27 owned transfers. All26 attacked destinations are owned in the next public observation. The86 debt-repaying moves comprise32 enemy attacks,5 neutral attacks and49 owned transfers. With all enclosing action-issued masks applied, V14 starts82 plans (52 direct/30 collection), continues156 plan moves, and issues86 collecting/152 deploying moves. Rejected parent starts are excluded.

## First change and later allocation

The useful concentrations at129 and142 remain unchanged. At193 debt3 defers the southern four-action collection toward(15,15). V14 instead captures(6,9) with8 from(7,9), captures neutral(9,8) with11 from(9,7), then captures(5,9) with6 from(6,9). Debt reaches0. The original southern donor sequence executes196–199, collecting3→5→6→7 and capturing(15,15), three turns later than V10's193–196 sequence.

Both public views and underlying19-field parent memory rejoin V10 at200–203 and206–224. The ledger remains distinct; this is not full20-field state equality. First opponent raw divergence is266. This reconvergence prevents treating the first193 veto alone as a sufficient explanation of the eventual loss.

Over the same first524 turns, V10 uses295 owned transfers/94 neutral attacks/123 enemy attacks; V14 uses306/79/127. Both pass12 times. Repayment performs real captures but does not reduce total transport or increase neutral expansion here. At450 V14 has84 land/360 army versus82/342; V10 has111/502 versus84/449. By523 V14 has73/356 versus100/336; V10 has101/451 versus99/405. These are evolving trajectories against an adaptive opponent, not isolated move effects.

All three build0 before524. V14 and V10-v6 own no castles throughout their episodes. V10 later builds seven castles, starting at655 (first visible as owned at656), then at908,918,925,944,987,1004. Its owned-castle count reaches7 at1005 and ends4. This later production gain is part of the longer winning trajectory, not an advantage already present before V14's524 loss.

## Terminal mechanism

At501–503 three deferrals route a15-army packet west from(8,16) through(8,15),(8,14),(8,13), growing to18; ordinary campaign moves it south at504. A seven-action collection505–511 gathers3→8 through row11 and captures enemy(14,10). Meanwhile the opponent's visible129 at(13,6) travels west then east along row12, reaching99 at(12,10) by513.

The19-army campaign packet at(9,13) moves west513–516 and captures(9,9), while the enemy travels east along row11. Enemy67 reaches(9,17) at523 and attacks home26 at(8,17), ending the game at524. Candidate actions521–523 are remote owned transfers. Incoming defender memory is inactive and `intercept_feasible` is false throughout500–523; this interval does not show a committed-defender release/restart loop. Death precedes deathtouch800: it is ordinary force/capture combat.

A useful next discrimination is whether serviced campaign moves assemble a relevant packet before a visible threat deadline. The data do not establish a safe new threshold or prove any particular alternative would rescue this game. More immediate captures and a repaid ledger did not preserve the winning trajectory.

## Integrity and limits

Candidate invalid/malformed0/0. Original Amin invalid actions:58 per V10,8 per V10-v6,13 per V14 (158 total); malformed0. Last V14 opponent invalid455; none during500–523. ## Next bounded question and evidence limits

The immediate scheduling hypothesis is falsified as a sufficient repair for Juraj: equal assembly/campaign service actually occurred but did not create enough neutral expansion or ensure the serviced packet completed a useful route. The next distinct question is explicit production-oriented candidate selection or packet service to a meaningful completion point, not another generic counter increment. A production candidate would need to execute a currently legal safe neutral capture (including source-screen safety), preserve useful active plans and terminal/defense/build priorities, and be tested against the known successful Amin collections. opponent_mechanism_audit:
# Operational opponent mechanisms and a bounded scheduling hypothesis

This audit reads the pinned Juraj V3.5 implementation, frozen Sentinel V6/V8 campaign logic, and complete retained public/action histories. No opponent source was copied into a policy, no inference or games ran, and no tracked source changed. Source identities and prior opening evidence are bound in `report.json`; the proposed action-debt ledger has independent full input bindings in `debt-audit.json`.

## 1. Separate action service for expansion and transport

Juraj `Agent::strategic_pick` (`main.cpp:41`) allocates soft decisions through persistent class credits, then ranks candidates inside the chosen class. `act` supplies a distinct neutral-expansion candidate set (`62`), changes expansion share with public land deficit (`50,65`), and tracks waiting expansion opportunities. It also gives production-tick proximity a bonus. Those are operational candidate/scheduling mechanisms, not merely prose in DESIGN.md.

Important limits of the implementation: all safe adjacent enemy attacks are tier1 at line52. Any tier0/1 candidate bypasses service credits, so the expansion-wait rule is not a universal guarantee. The neutral-expansion generator at62 does not call the ordinary `safe_step` counterattack predicate. Named Budget fields (`core.hpp:34–35`) largely gate eligibility; they do not partition all real packets into disjoint accounts. Do not import these details as proven safety or optimal scheduling.

Our V8 instead picks one enemy objective by defending force plus structure bonuses (`sentinel_v8_agent.py:84–91`), finds the cheapest sufficient collection for that objective, and lets its eligible plan override the V6 campaign (`204–207`). There is no separate action-service accounting for expansion or the underlying campaign. V6's underlying score (`sentinel_agent.py:154–163`) values immediate capture and moving army together; it has no persistent multi-role scheduling debt either.

The actual original V10/Juraj case12 action census supports a concrete resource-allocation gap:

|Turns|V10 owned transfers / neutral attempts / enemy attempts|Juraj owned transfers / neutral attempts / enemy attempts|Next land, V10 vs Juraj|
|---|---|---|---|
|100–149|31 /4 /15|23 /16 /11|42 vs51|
|150–199|33 /2 /15|18 /16 /16|42 vs69|
|200–249|27 /2 /21|16 /22 /12|53 vs82|

These categories come from each acting player's current public destination and raw action. They are attempts, not guaranteed captures or an inferred internal Juraj scheduler trace. They show sustained neutral-income underinvestment and transport cost in our actual losing trajectory. Neither bot built before422, so speculative castle planning does not explain this particular early production lead. Twelve early Sentinel passes versus24 Juraj passes likewise show that minimizing PASS alone is not the right objective.

## 2. Existing packets move toward a front and can keep operating after one capture

Juraj's `act:63` chooses a strategic sink from the known general, an active contact front, or a belief target; it scores existing safe surplus by graph ETA. `reconcile`/`commit_packet` (`36–38`) retain packet identity, target/role and observed location, while `packet_route_ok`/`route_allowed` (`40`, `core.hpp:33`) restrict nonprogress and short cycles. Immediate combat and expansion candidates remain available when the packet reaches contact. This is not a global optimal logistics planner: front identity can change, its reserves are approximate, and its terrain routes do not predict enemy merges. Packet bookkeeping alone does not prove scheduling priority.

V8's sufficient-force calculation is explicitly one-objective accounting (`104–124`); its plan clears when the objective attack is issued (`209–220`). Its first capture can be earlier but its remaining force too small for an efficient sequence. In the bound common opening, V6 sends the existing8 at(9,17) through eight real owned transfers, arriving16 at(11,11) on108, then captures seven tiles at108–115. V10's smaller100–104 collection captures the first enemy tile four turns sooner and holds it22 observations. Its106–110 second collection also captures and holds67 observations. Those plans are useful; they nevertheless defer the same large-packet route by15 turns. Through123, V6 has15 actual captures on9 transfers versus V10's7 captures on17 transfers. A first-target force/ETA test misses follow-through and competing-packet opportunity cost.

The immediate lesson is to schedule productive campaign work against assembly, not to label all collection wasteful. Explicit multi-capture/front valuation would be a separate, more complex candidate: bounded current-visible reach/force accounting for a small fixed set of existing packets, not all donor-target pairs. It must not assume that future fog cells are empty or that a captured target retains its old enemy force. Keep this separate from the simpler debt test below.

## Bounded action-debt candidate: mechanism, exact passive schedule, risks

Root's proposed independent scheduler can add one scalar debt to the existing parent memory. Charge one for each actually issued collection transfer, including the move arriving at the rally. Repay one, floor zero, on an actually issued underlying V6 campaign move. Do not repay for deployment, defense, pursuit, mobilization, builds or PASS. While debt is positive, defer only a NEW collection to a real V6 campaign proposal; preserve existing plans, direct deployment and higher priorities. Do not bank negative credit or charge a parent collection whose action was replaced. Returned parent transport memory must reflect the issued fallback.

This changes action service rather than target ranking and does not invent an ETA cutoff. The1:1 ratio is an unvalidated experimental setting, not a value proven by opponent code or data. Full enabled-state JIT memory should retain a fixed twentieth scalar; disabled action/telemetry and projected19-leaf base-memory parity must be explicit.

The completed passive ledger uses original actual-action masks and excludes intercept/commitment defense events from repayment. It finds:

* Juraj:100–102 collection charges produce debt3; deployment103–104 and direct105 leave it3; the first deferred new collection is106. On the unchanged original history,111–116 campaign moves repay all6 accumulated units, and129 starts at zero.
* Amin game1: useful129 and142 start debt-free, but the first deferred collection is193 with debt3. This is the same known first V13 preservation-risk fixture. Its historical four-action collection captures enemy1 at196 with5 and retains63 observations. Preserving129/142 does not establish preserved winning behavior.
* my_bot9 game4: first deferred new collection105 has debt3, after the100 collection. This is an earlier and different first change from the successful V13 trajectory's immediate capture100.

Only each prefix up to its FIRST deferred start is a candidate-consistent history. The passive ledger continues charging original actions afterward for descriptive comparison; later zero/nonzero admissions are not predictions of an adaptive candidate. The script excludes actual override/guard and commitment events conservatively; some held-screen frames can still perform economically useful campaign work, so source attribution must be defined precisely in implementation.

The debt rule does not guarantee neutral expansion: V6 repayment itself can be owned transport or enemy attack, and direct deployments remain unbounded. A growing land deficit could persist. Conversely, a useful sequence of collections may deserve consecutive service, while debt forces unrelated campaign moves. Existing Amin193/292 captures, defensive collection interruption506, ready direct163, and high-value structure/general plans are necessary counterexamples. If adding exclusions for structures, make that a declared design choice before tests rather than reacting to results.

Runtime cost should be scalar bookkeeping beyond the parent and one existing V6 fallback evaluation when a new collection is deferred. A straightforward JAX wrapper may still compute the fallback graph every frame; no throughput promise follows from counting scalar fields. Reusing the V6 proposal would avoid duplicate solves but requires a reviewed extraction contract. Benchmark representative first-block fixtures in the official runtime, check both disabled parity and actual memory reconciliation, then compare complete adaptive games. No runtime measurement or new candidate is claimed here.

The alternative neutral-expansion scheduler addresses the measured income gap more directly but introduces its own safe-capture selection and admission policy. Testing it alongside debt would mix mechanisms. The debt candidate is a bounded first test of assembly-versus-campaign starvation; if it fails, the full neutral-service discrepancy remains evidence for a separate campaign redesign, not another single-capture veto.
